## Historical audit: S0288

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/test/bw_0011/2/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; observations are unsplit.

**Goal versus evidence.** The requested goal was a view-matched, editable 3D reconstruction from one RGB image, not an independently calibrated scene (line 1, `model_request`). The student’s inventory *interpreted* it as a clean laboratory with blue walls, cabinet, dandelion mural, display and ceiling; those labels are not independent image verification (line 3, H `model_response`).

| Stage | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H emitted separate named architecture, cabinet, mural, display and ceiling assets, with cabinet frames, shelves and handles. The mural used geometric stems and rays rather than an image texture; colored surfaces, glazing opacity, camera and lights were specified. The program estimated about 235 primitives (lines 3–4). This establishes multiple modeled objects and hierarchical membership, not correct physical connections or visibility. No articulated pose was described. |
| Validation and revision | Step 1 built and rendered successfully (lines 6, 8–9); the reference and render were supplied for comparison (line 11). H reported a corner too far right, excessive return-wall extent, washed-out surfaces and a light ceiling. It shortened the return, changed camera, colors and lighting, and rebuilt cabinet and mural details (lines 13–14). These are H’s visual judgments, not independent verification. Step 2 also built and rendered successfully (lines 16, 18–19). |
| Final revision | After receiving the second render (line 21), H reported the corner still too far right, wall too tall, mural nearly blank and cabinet windows too pale and rectangular. It changed camera position, target and lens, darkened cabinet panels, strengthened mural geometry and removed a fill light (lines 23–24). Step 3 built and rendered successfully; the runner selected it (lines 26, 28–30). No subsequent inspection or `DONE` is visible. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student feedback is visible. The system’s general reconstruction and review instructions were received, and the runner supplied execution results and images; H’s diagnoses and revisions are its own observable responses, not evidence of teacher adoption. The sessions recorded no autonomous tool calls, although H independently produced three programs and revised them between runner executions (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is a **technical build/render success with visual correctness unknown**, not a demonstrated formal scene-match success or an empty patch. The audit has no image pixels to inspect; neither the student’s descriptions nor successful renders establish object coverage, material fidelity, spatial connections, camera alignment or lighting quality. The final render was not visibly reviewed. Code requested 48 Cycles samples, while render logs report 16, so effective runner settings differed; the cause is not shown (lines 24, 29). Whether the stronger mural or revised framing improved the match remains unresolved.

**Lessons.** Transferable: separate execution success from visual validation, and preserve editable parts while iterating from rendered feedback. Task-specific: the reported corner, cabinet and mural discrepancies motivated these particular parameter changes; their diagnoses and effectiveness remain hypotheses.
